transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, I guess I came in because... well, since I tried to clean up my image and my daily routine for some arts board stuff I'm involved with, I’ve just been a lot more tense and down than I expected to be. 

I mean, I’m still doing the basics and getting through the day, but I keep dropping these little things that I normally really care about—like my fair planning notes or my design drafts. And then I just feel guilty about falling behind, and instead of actually catching up on the work, I just end up canceling plans with people. It's just been really frustrating.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about two months now. Basically, it started right around the time I tried to overhaul my daily routine and my overall presentation.
Over these past two months, have you felt a persistent sense of sadness or a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, no, I wouldn't say it's every day, or for most of the day. It's not really a constant sadness. It's more like... I just get down when I think about the things I'm dropping or when I feel overwhelmed by my routine. 

And I haven't really lost interest in the things I normally enjoy. I still care about my art and everything, I just feel a bit too tense or distracted to actually sit down and focus on it right now. So it's not like a persistent everyday thing, just more tied to when I'm feeling stressed about falling behind.
Outside of this recent period of trying to overhaul your routine, would you say you generally find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of different things in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I'll worry about normal things here and there, but I wouldn't say I worry excessively about a bunch of different stuff. Before I started trying to change up my routine, I was actually pretty relaxed. It's really just been this recent situation that's got me feeling so tense.
When you feel 'down' about falling behind, do you experience any physical symptoms like crying spells, or do you feel a sense of hopelessness or worthlessness?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or anything like that. And I don't really have crying spells either. It's just... I get frustrated with myself. Like, I'll feel bummed out that I'm not keeping up, but I don't feel worthless. It's just annoying, you know? I know I can do better, I'm just struggling to actually do it right now.
When you feel 'down' about your situation, do you notice that your mood feels noticeably low or sad, rather than just feeling frustrated or tense?

Um, no, not really. I mean, it's not like a deep sadness or feeling really low. It's mostly just... I get frustrated. I feel tense and annoyed that I'm not doing what I set out to do, but I wouldn't really call it feeling sad.
Even though you wouldn't describe your mood as 'sad' or 'low,' have you noticed any periods where you have felt a sense of emptiness or a lack of emotional spark, even if it's brief?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I don't feel empty, and I wouldn't say I've lost my emotional spark or anything. It really is just... frustration. I still care about things, I just get annoyed when I don't stick to my plans.
When you feel this tension or frustration, do you experience physical sensations like a racing heart, muscle tension, or feeling like you are on edge?

Um, no, not really a racing heart or anything extreme like that. I guess I do feel a little on edge sometimes, just because I'm annoyed with myself, but it's not like my muscles are super tense or anything physical like that. It's just more of a mental frustration, I think.
When you feel this frustration and tension, do you find yourself feeling worried or anxious about the future consequences of not keeping up with your plans?

No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around worrying about the future or anything like that. It's not an anxious feeling. I'm just annoyed in the moment that I didn't do what I was supposed to do. I don't really think about the long-term consequences, I just get mad at myself right then.
